claim.note: Printed as a section heading (like 6.1 IDENTIFICATION DIVISION and 6.3 DATA DIVISION, both '## ' in the markdown) but transcribed as a plain paragraph with no heading marker; its subsections are then promoted: '## 6.2.1 General Description', '## 6.2.2 Organization', '## 6.2.3 Structure' sit at level 2 where 6.1.1-6.1.3 are level 3 (###).
claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) breaks the document outline that section lookups and citation checks navigate by; the clause becomes unfindable by its number or is filed under the wrong parent.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page IV-31 (PDF p177) opens with the section heading '6.2 ENVIRONMENT DIVISION' on its own line above '6.2.1 General Description', '6.2.2 Organization' and '6.2.3 Structure'. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 7430 it is a plain paragraph with no '#' marker, while its siblings are headings ('## 6.1 IDENTIFICATION DIVISION' at line 7398, '## 6.3 DATA DIVISION' at line 7480), and its children are at '##' (lines 7432, 7436, 7444) where 6.1.1-6.1.3 and 6.3.1-6.3.2 are '###'. The text is present, but the outline is wrong: 6.2 has no heading node, and 6.2.1-6.2.3 sit as siblings of 6.1 and 6.3. That is a real structural defect for heading-based navigation. The claim describes it accurately.
